overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: public participation is discretionary for the chair, and the Council's live stream gave adequate alternative access. It recommended, as best practice only, clarifying shared-account speaker procedures.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council removed a member of the public from its Sept. 22 Zoom meeting after he made remarks during public participation.
allegations.key_passage: In this case, as public participation is discretionary, we find no violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council did not permit her to participate in the Sept. 22 meeting, though she had registered to speak; the shared Zoom account led to her removal.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body allow public participation during its meetings

allegations.summary: Whether live Zoom-only participation with a removal left the public without adequate alternative access to the Sept. 22 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Council provided “adequate alternative” means of access for member of the public to observe the September 22 meeting through the Lowell TeleMedia Center live stream.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
